Rashi on Niddah 21a:11:1.hebrew: לא אמרינן כו' - דקסברי אין רוב חתיכות של ארבע מיני דמים, דלא אתחזק לן האי רובא:
Rashi on Niddah 21a:11:1.english: We do not say, etc. - For they hold that the majority of pieces are not of the four types of blood, as this majority has not been established for us.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:12:1.hebrew: ירוקה ולבנה - לאו מארבע מיני דמים הן, אלא אדום, וכמימי אדמה, וכקרן כרכום, וכמזוג. ושחור לא קא חשיב, דהיינו אדום, אלא שלקה:
Rashi on Niddah 21a:12:1.english: Green or white - They are not among the four types of blood; rather, [the four are] red, like earth water, like the tip of a saffron crocus, and like diluted [wine]. And [he] does not count black, as that is red, only that it deteriorated.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:14:1.english: For whom does it teach it - That is to say, to make known whose opinion it comes [to teach].

Rashi on Niddah 21a:15:1.english: Rather, for Rabbi Yehuda - To make known that regarding green and white as well, he disagrees.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:16:1.hebrew: ותו לרבי יוחנן וכו' - כלומר, הך קושיא דירוקה ולבנה לא איבעי לן לפרושי, דכי היכי דקשיא ליה לשמואל קשיא ליה לרבי יוחנן, דהא רבי יוחנן נמי אמר על שאר מינין לרבי יהודה טהורה, והכא קתני ירוקה ולבנה ופליג רבי יהודה. ותו קשיא אחריתי לר' יוחנן, דאמר של ארבעת מיני דמים דברי הכל כו':
Rashi on Niddah 21a:16:1.english: And furthermore, to Rabbi Yoḥanan, etc. - That is to say: There was no need for us to explain this difficulty regarding [a piece that is] green and white, since just as it is difficult for Shmuel, it is difficult for Rabbi Yoḥanan, for Rabbi Yoḥanan also said that with regard to other colors, according to Rabbi Yehuda she is pure, yet here [the baraita] teaches green and white, and Rabbi Yehuda disagrees. And furthermore, [there is] another difficulty for Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said: "[A piece] of the four types of blood, all agree [that she is impure]," etc.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:17:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: וכי תימא כי פליגי רבנן אירוקה ולבנה, אלא אדומה ושחורה למאן קתני לה? כו', אלא לאו רבנן ופליגי:
Rashi on Niddah 21a:17:1.english: This is how we read: "And if you would say: When the Rabbis disagree, [it is] regarding green and white, but [then] for whose [opinion] does [the baraita] teach red and black? etc. Rather, is it not [for] the Rabbis, and they disagree?"

Rashi on Niddah 21a:19:1.english: Opening of the grave - [Meaning] the womb.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:19:2.hebrew: בלא דם - דם לידה. הלכך לרבנן, כי ליכא דם — טהורה, ואפילו החתיכה של ארבע מיני דמים, דחתיכה לאו דם הוא אלא בשר, ולא אמר: דם אחר איכא ואנן הוא דלא חזינן, דקסברי רבנן: אפשר לפתיחת הקבר בלא דם. לר' יהודה, אפילו ירוקה ולבנה — טמאה, דודאי דם אחר הוה ואנן הוא דלא חזינן, דאי אפשר לפתיחת הקבר בלא דם:
Rashi on Niddah 21a:19:2.english: Without blood - [Namely,] blood of childbirth. Therefore, according to the Rabbis, when there is no blood, she is pure, and even if the piece is of [one of] the four types of [impure] blood, for a piece [of tissue] is not blood, but rather flesh, and we do not say: "There is other blood, and it is [just] that we did not see it," for the Rabbis maintain that opening of the womb is possible without blood. According to Rabbi Yehuda, even [if it is] green or white, she is impure, for certainly there was other blood, and it is [just] that we did not see it, for opening of the womb is impossible without blood.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:19:3.hebrew: קשתה שנים - בתוך י"א יום שבין נדה לנדה, וראתה דם מחמת קושי:
Rashi on Niddah 21a:19:3.english: She experienced difficult labor for two [days] - Within the eleven days between [one period of] niddah and [another], and she saw blood due to the difficulty [of labor].

Rashi on Niddah 21a:19:4.english: And on the third [day] she miscarried - And she does not know whether she saw blood during that birth or not.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:19:5.hebrew: ואינה יודעת - אם נפל הוא, ואם רוח בעלמא הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 21a:19:5.english: And she does not know - Whether it was a miscarried fetus, or whether it was merely wind.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:1:1.english: The Sharon [wine] - [That is, when it is] diluted.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:1:2.english: Is judged like undiluted Carmelite [wine] - For they also examine [blood] with undiluted Carmelite [wine]. And some read: "The Carmelite [wine] is judged like the Sharon [wine]."

Rashi on Niddah 21a:2:1.hebrew: בכוס טבריא של זכוכית פשוט - טנב"ש, ואיידי דקליש, נראה בו אדמומית היין:
Rashi on Niddah 21a:2:1.english: In a simple Tiberian cup of glass - [*Tenves*, meaning thin], and since it is thin, the redness of the wine is visible in it.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:4:1.english: [A woman] who discharges a piece [of flesh], if there is blood with it, she is impure - On account of [the impurity of] a niddah.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:4:2.hebrew: ואם לאו טהורה - דלאו לידה היא, דאי לידה הויא, בלא דם נמי טמאה, דכתיב (ויקרא י״ב:ב׳) כימי נדת דותה תטמא:
Rashi on Niddah 21a:4:2.english: And if not, she is pure - For it is not [considered] a birth; for if it were a birth, she would be impure even without blood, as it is written (Leviticus 12:2): "As in the days of her menstrual infirmity she shall be impure."

Rashi on Niddah 21a:4:3.english: Rabbi Yehuda says, etc. - [This is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:5:3.hebrew: אם נימוחו טמאה - משום נדה, דדם הוא:
Rashi on Niddah 21a:5:3.english: If they dissolved, she is ritually impure - On account of [being a] niddah, because it is blood.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:6:1.hebrew: מין דגים - נמי לאו ולד הוא, וטעמא מפרש בגמרא. הלכך, אי איכא דם — טמאה נדה, ואם לאו — טהורה:
Rashi on Niddah 21a:6:1.english: A species of fish - Is also not an offspring, and the reason is explained in the Gemara. Therefore, if there is blood, she is impure as a niddah, and if not, she is pure.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:7:1.hebrew: תשב לזכר - ימי טומאת שבעה, וימי טהרה ל"ג, וכל דמים שתראה בהן טהורין:
Rashi on Niddah 21a:7:1.english: She shall observe [the periods] for a male - The days of impurity are seven, and the days of purity are thirty-three, and all blood that she sees during them is pure.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:8:1.hebrew: לזכר ולנקבה - לחומרא: ימי טומאה דנקבה שבועים, וימי טוהר כלים לסוף ארבעים יום כזכר, ולא פ' כנקבה. ובגמרא מפרש: מאי שנא דלחיה ועוף קרי ולד יותר מדגים:
Rashi on Niddah 21a:8:1.english: For a male and for a female - [This is] as a stringency: The days of impurity are [those of] a female, two weeks; and the days of purity terminate at the end of forty days like a male, and not eighty like a female. And in the Gemara it explains what is different about a wild animal and a bird, that [Rabbi Meir] calls [them] an offspring more than fish.

Rashi on Niddah 21a:9:1.hebrew: של ד' מיני דמים - דקסבר היא גופה דם, הלכך טמאה נדה, אבל ולד לא הוי:
Rashi on Niddah 21a:9:1.english: Of the four types of blood - For he holds that [the piece] itself is blood; therefore, she is impure as a niddah, but it is not an offspring.

Tosafot on Niddah 21a:11:1.hebrew: ורבנן סברי לא אמרינן רוב חתיכות - תימה: ונימא דהוה פלגא ופלגא, ויהא ודאי טמא ברה"י, אע"ג דאיכא חזקת טהרה? וי"ל, דאמרי' לעיל (נדה דף יח:) דאפילו לרבי יהודה לא הוי רוב גמור, ואין שורפין עליו את התרומה; ולרבנן אפילו פלגא לא הוי, ואדרבה, רוב החתיכות לאו של ד' מיני דמים הם:
Tosafot on Niddah 21a:11:1.english: And the Rabbis hold: We do not say [that] the majority of pieces [are of the four types of blood] - [This is] astonishing: Let us say that it is half and half [an even doubt], and let it be definitely impure in a private domain (bi-reshut ha-yachid), even though there is a presumption of purity (chazakat taharah)? And one can say that we say above (Niddah 18b) that even according to Rabbi Yehuda it is not a complete majority, and one does not burn teruma on account of it; and according to the Rabbis, it is not even half, and on the contrary, the majority of pieces are not of the four types of blood.

Tosafot on Niddah 21a:16:1.hebrew: לרבי יוחנן אדומה ושחורה למאן קתני לה אי לרבי יהודה - וה"פ: המפלת אדומה ושחורה דינו כדמפרש ר' יהודה בסיפא, השתא ירוקה כו'. ומתוך פי' ר"ח משמע דל"ג וכ"ת כי פליגי רבנן אירוקה ולבנה; וכן נראה, דהא בהדיא קתני במילתייהו שחורה ואדומה, ואין זו סוגיית הש"ס:
Tosafot on Niddah 21a:16:1.english: According to Rabbi Yoḥanan, for whom does [the baraita] teach red and black? If [you say] for Rabbi Yehuda - And this is the explanation: [If one suggests that in the case of a woman] who discharges a red or black [piece of tissue], the ruling is as Rabbi Yehuda explains in the latter clause, [the Gemara challenges:] "Now, [if for] green, etc. [and white she is impure, is red and black necessary?]" And from the commentary of Rabbeinu Chananel it is implied that we do not read: "And if you would say: when the Rabbis disagree, [it is] regarding green and white"; and so it appears [correct], for behold, [the baraita] explicitly teaches in their statement "black and red", and this is not the way of the Talmud's discussion.

Tosafot on Niddah 21a:9:1.hebrew: אלא בחתיכה של ד' מיני דמים - דקסבר ר' יהודה, דם נדות הוא, ונקרש ונעשה חתיכה, כדאמר לקמן גבי מפלת מין דגים; ורבנן סברי, מקור מגדל חתיכה, ולא דם נדות הוא:
Tosafot on Niddah 21a:9:1.english: Only in [the case of] a piece of the four types of blood - For Rabbi Yehuda holds [that] it is blood of niddah, and it congealed and became a piece [of tissue], as [the Gemara] says below regarding [a woman who] discharges a species of fish; and the Rabbis hold [that] the womb grows a piece [of tissue], and it is not blood of niddah.
